hero.headline: Martin County Sheriff's Office seeks public help finding missing 14-year-old autistic boy in Palm City
hero.teaser: The Martin County Sheriff's Office is asking for the public's help in locating Ethan Boyd, a 14-year-old autistic boy who went missing Wednesday in Palm City.
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office is asking for the public's help in locating Ethan Boyd, a 14-year-old autistic boy who went missing Wednesday in Palm City. Ethan was last seen at 5:20 p.m. Wednesday running toward the south side of the Grand Oaks senior living community near Coquina Cove.

Ethan is described as 5 feet 7 inches tall, weighing approximately 130 pounds, with brown hair. He was last seen wearing a dark blue shirt and seafoam green shorts without shoes.

The sheriff's office is urging anyone who sees or has seen Ethan to contact them immediately. The Grand Oaks Living Facility is located in Palm City near Coquina Cove.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Martin County Sheriff's Office immediately at 772-220-7170 or call 911.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce King's Landing developer asks city for six more months, reports $15 million funding shortfall
cards.teaser: The developer behind Fort Pierce's King's Landing project told city commissioners Monday it needs roughly $15 million more to complete the development's hotel and is requesting ano
cards.body:
The developer behind Fort Pierce's King's Landing project told city commissioners Monday it needs roughly $15 million more to complete the development's hotel and is requesting another 180 days to secure the funding. Live Oak CEO Paul Bertozzi said the shortfall stems largely from rising construction costs since the project's budget was first set. Commissioners did not vote on the request but scheduled a special meeting for September 14 to decide whether to grant the extension or take other action.

King's Landing is planned for the site of the former H.D. King Power Plant on the Fort Pierce waterfront and would include a hotel, condominiums, restaurants, retail space and public waterfront access. The project has changed hands multiple times since the city first selected Audubon Development to build it in 2019, most recently passing to Live Oak in 2025. City officials say the development agreement has already been amended three times to adjust deadlines and financing terms. Bertozzi told commissioners he is already in talks with potential investors and expects at least one to be part of the September presentation.

Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky said he will not support further delay, noting the city's financial exposure has already grown with the property's value as a city incentive rising from about $2.5 million to $8.5 million over time. Commissioner Michael Broderick took the opposite view, saying that terminating the agreement and reclaiming the property could mean years of litigation and cost the city hundreds of thousands of dollars, on top of the time needed to find a new developer and restart construction. The city attorney confirmed Monday that Live Oak is currently in breach of its development agreement over missed deadlines.

Bertozzi explained that hotel financing typically requires a 65-35 split between bank loans and investor equity, and that rising interest and construction costs widened the amount Live Oak needs to raise privately as the project's overall budget increased. While the funding gap continues for the hotel portion of King's Landing, homes are currently under construction next door with a different developer. Commissioners will revisit the issue at the September 14 special meeting, followed by a Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency board meeting the next day, since both bodies must approve any changes to the three-party development agreement.

cards.headline: State lawmaker challenges Fort Pierce Causeway Cove development over zoning compliance
cards.teaser: State Rep. Dana Trabulsy told Fort Pierce city commissioners Monday that the proposed Causeway Cove development does not meet the zoning requirements of the Live Local Act, raising questions about the massive waterfront project.
cards.body:
State Rep. Dana Trabulsy told Fort Pierce city commissioners Monday that the proposed Causeway Cove development does not meet the zoning requirements of Florida's Live Local Act, the same law she supported in 2023 that allows developers to bypass local height and density restrictions. The Causeway Cove project would transform the existing Causeway Cove Marina into a mixed-use development featuring more than 900 apartments and condos, restaurants, and a hotel tower reaching nearly 200 feet in height.

Trabulsy said a mapping error incorrectly designated portions of the Causeway Cove site as commercial zoning when they should be classified as aquatic development. The Live Local Act permits developers to exceed local height and density limits only in commercial and mixed-use zones, provided they dedicate 40% of residential units to affordable housing for at least 30 years. The aquatic development zoning classification would prevent the project from utilizing Live Local Act provisions, potentially forcing developers to comply with Fort Pierce's original height and density restrictions.

Fort Pierce City Commissioner Michael Broderick questioned whether such a significant zoning issue would have escaped state oversight during the approval process. When Trabulsy urged commissioners to rescind the project's approval and pursue legal action, Broderick expressed skepticism about the city's chances of success in court, saying he does not see an angle of attack that would not cost the city hundreds of thousands of dollars, if not millions of dollars, to fight.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police release 911 call in fatal domestic shooting of Palm Beach Sheriff's Office employee
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police released the 911 call made the night Elizabeth Ortega, 50, was shot and killed outside her home on the 2000 block of SE Oxmoor Terrace, where suspect Ralph Va
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police released the 911 call made the night Elizabeth Ortega, 50, was shot and killed outside her home on the 2000 block of SE Oxmoor Terrace, where suspect Ralph Varela Sr., 50, was later found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. In the 911 call, a neighbor described hearing five or six gunshots loud enough to rattle her house before her 4-year-old child spotted Ortega lying motionless in the front yard. The caller told the dispatcher she did not go outside because she was frightened, and that Ortega and her husband were frequently heard arguing.

The caller said both vehicles belonging to the residents were still parked outside the home and that Ortega was not moving. Responding officers found Ortega suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. She was airlifted to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she later died. Police said Varela returned inside the home after the shooting, where officers later found him dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Palm Beach Sheriff's Office said Ortega's son, Ralph Varela Jr., is a firefighter with Palm Beach County Fire Rescue, and asked the community to keep both agencies in their thoughts. The investigation remains active as detectives continue processing evidence and await final results from the Medical Examiner's Office. Funeral arrangements are pending.

Port St. Lucie police extended their condolences to Ortega's family and loved ones. The department encouraged anyone experiencing domestic violence to ask for help and seek help.

cards.headline: Florida property tax amendment draws organized opposition while supporters remain quiet
cards.teaser: A proposed constitutional amendment to cut property taxes in Florida is facing mounting organized opposition while support remains largely silent. Groups representing police, firef
cards.body:
A proposed constitutional amendment to cut property taxes in Florida is facing mounting organized opposition while support remains largely silent. Groups representing police, firefighters, sheriffs, hospitals, cities and counties have raised alarms about Amendment 3, warning the proposed tax cut could hollow out local budgets and jeopardize police, fire, emergency medical and other services. The Republican-controlled Legislature placed Amendment 3 on the November ballot during a June special session. Under the proposal, the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes would increase to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. The amendment would also reduce the annual assessment-growth cap on non-homestead properties from 10% to 5%. A state fiscal analysis estimates the amendments quantifiable provisions would reduce local property-tax collections by nearly $4.93 billion during the 2027-28 fiscal year, eventually reaching approximately $11.83 billion annually.

Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd called the proposal a train wreck during a Tuesday news conference. The Florida Sheriffs Association said it is significantly concerned about the proposal. The Florida State Fraternal Order of Police has formally opposed it, while the Florida Professional Firefighters and Florida Fire Chiefs Association warned that it could undermine public-safety funding without providing a replacement revenue source. On Wednesday, the No On Three campaign announced endorsements from 31 Democratic state lawmakers, including House Democratic Leader Fentrice Driskell and Senate Democratic Leader Lori Berman.

Governor Ron DeSantis called the special session that produced the proposal and said he will vote for it, but made clear the Legislature's final product fell short of what he wanted. Attorney General James Uthmeier paired support for tax relief with concern about potential consequences. U.S. Senator Rick Scott initially appeared skeptical but later announced he would vote for Amendment 3. No comparable statewide Yes On Three campaign has publicly materialized.

A July University of North Florida poll found 61% support when likely voters were told the amendment would begin phasing out non-school homestead taxes, only one percentage point above the 60% constitutional threshold needed to pass. Support fell to 45% when respondents were also told that estimates suggested the proposal could create an approximately $11.8 billion municipal budget shortfall over its first two years. Leon County Circuit Judge David Frank ruled this week that the title and summary written by lawmakers were biased, misleading and factually inaccurate, ordering Attorney General Uthmeier to submit a replacement within 10 days.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police seek driver in hit-and-run that injured two children in crosswalk
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are investigating a hit-and-run crash at North 25th Street and Avenue M where an early-2000s gold Mercedes-Benz struck two children in a marked crosswalk before the driver fled the scene.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police are investigating a hit-and-run crash that injured two children who were crossing a street in a marked crosswalk. The crash happened at North 25th Street and Avenue M, where an early-2000s gold Mercedes-Benz was turning from Avenue M onto North 25th Street when it struck the children. The driver initially stopped and checked on the children before fleeing the scene.

The driver is described as a Black male between 20 and 30 years old. The car is described as a gold Mercedes-Benz with a tan interior, no window tint and damage to the driver's side. Police said one child was transported to a local hospital and later flown to St. Mary's Medical Center in West Palm Beach, where they were treated for non-life-threatening injuries.

The investigation remains active. Anyone with information regarding the vehicle or driver is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.

cards.headline: Property tax increases push Treasure Coast resident to relocate to Puerto Rico
cards.teaser: A Treasure Coast man said rising property taxes in Florida pushed him to leave the state and buy a home in Puerto Rico, where he pays nothing in property taxes. Jock Tate now lives
cards.body:
A Treasure Coast man said rising property taxes in Florida pushed him to leave the state and buy a home in Puerto Rico, where he pays nothing in property taxes. Jock Tate now lives in Salinas, Puerto Rico, in a 3-bedroom home he purchased for $95,000. As a disabled veteran, he qualifies for exemptions that eliminate his property tax bill entirely.

 Tate said the price of housing in Puerto Rico is much less than Florida, especially South Florida. He said property taxes were going up and he could not afford it anymore.

 His move comes as Florida homeowners face rising property tax burdens across the state. According to a Florida Tax Watch study, property taxes rose 146.2% in St. Lucie County between 2014 and 2024. Other Treasure Coast counties saw similar increases: 131.5% in Okeechobee County, 99.4% in Palm Beach County, 90.1% in Indian River County and 90.1% in Martin County.

 Florida voters will have a chance to weigh in on property taxes this November. A referendum on the ballot would raise the Homestead Exemption, lowering property tax bills for Florida homeowners. Many city and county officials have warned that rolling back property taxes would lead to budget cuts and force local governments to raise other fees and taxes to offset lost revenue.

cards.headline: Three candidates vie for Martin County Commission District 4 seat in August 18 primary
cards.teaser: Three candidates are running for the District 4 Martin County Commission seat in the August 18 Primary Election. John Dial, Sarah Heard, and John Kaz Kazanjian qualified for the ra
cards.body:
Three candidates are running for the District 4 Martin County Commission seat in the August 18 Primary Election. John Dial, Sarah Heard, and John Kaz Kazanjian qualified for the race.

 Dial identified over-development as the most serious issue facing Martin County, citing Senate Bill 180, SB102, and new mandates from Tallahassee that remove power from local voters and leaders. He said he would go to Tallahassee as often as necessary to represent local control and push to restore the county's ability to make decisions. Dial also opposed using taxpayer money to fund Brightline, calling it a private company that is not U.S.-owned, carries roughly $2 billion in debt, and is reportedly losing more than $220 million a year. He said he would be open to a train station if a private rail company wanted to invest its own capital, or a fair market land lease at the fairgrounds provided the property would revert to the county if the company fails.

 Heard said the legislature is taking decision-making out of the Board's hands and only essential services like the Sheriff and Fire Rescue can be funded with ad valorem taxes. She said even if funding only public safety, the county would not be able to fund it by the third year. Heard said she is in favor of a train station downtown but would consider the fairgrounds location if the majority of residents overwhelmingly favors it. She said she does not want to see data centers in unincorporated Martin County because they are not allowed uses on agricultural lands, and a comprehensive plan amendment would have to be approved to change the future land use, which she would oppose.

 Both Dial and Heard addressed a potential referendum on raising the Homestead exemption and cutting ad valorem property tax income. Dial said he would protect essential services first including fire protection, law enforcement, waste management, and education while reviewing non-essential programs and discretionary spending for reductions. He also suggested exploring ways to turn costly county assets like Sailfish Splash, the golf course, and the cafe on the beach into revenue-producing opportunities by leasing them to private operators.

 On the Business Development Board's annual $450,000 funding, which District 1 Commissioner Eileen Vargas opposed on June 23, Dial said he supports the BDB in its current role but that every use of taxpayer dollars must be examined carefully if spending cuts are forced. Heard agreed that the BDB is too dependent on government funding.

cards.headline: Vero Beach keeps millage flat at 2.98 mills, adds $410,000 to budget for police positions
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach City Council set a preliminary millage rate for the 2026-27 fiscal year at the current 2.9816 mills during a July 22 budget workshop, approving a $37,352,589 budget
cards.body:
The Vero Beach City Council set a preliminary millage rate for the 2026-27 fiscal year at the current 2.9816 mills during a July 22 budget workshop, approving a $37,352,589 budget that includes $410,000 transferred from the General Fund's unassigned fund balance to cover salaries for three vacant police officer positions. City Manager Monte Falls told the council the city holds a strong financial position with a total General Fund balance of $54 million, including $17.7 million in unassigned funds and $35.56 million in committed reserves.

 Falls recommended using $435,160 from the unassigned balance to offset the city's Other Post Employee Benefit trust payment, which would allow the vacant police positions to be filled. For a Vero Beach homeowner with a property assessed at $300,000, a $50,000 Homestead Exemption and a Save Our Homes 3 percent increase, the current millage rate would result in about $25 a year in additional ad valorem tax, Falls said.

 Vice Mayor Linda Moore and Councilmember Taylor Dingle raised concerns about funding recurring positions with non-recurring money, particularly with Amendment 3 on the November ballot potentially creating a $1.3 million budget hole. Mayor John Cotugno said Vero Beach would fare better than other Florida communities if Amendment 3 passes because the city has four enterprise funds and a diversified tax base including industrial, residential and commercial revenue sources.

 After debate, the council approved adding the $410,000 to the budget by offsetting capital expenses already included in the operating budget. Falls told Hometown News on Sept. 27 that the new police officer salaries would actually cost the city an extra $300,000. The council will return in September to set the final millage rate and adopt the budget.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce gets 90-day extension to pay state fines for Little Jim's dock violations
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection extended the city's deadline to Sept. 15 to review a proposed consent order resolving nearly $16,000 in state fines tied to docks at Little Jim Bait & Tackle.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection gave Fort Pierce until Sept. 15 to review, approve and submit a proposed consent order resolving nearly $16,000 in state fines tied to docks at Little Jim Bait & Tackle. The state agency extended the city's deadline by 90 days, meaning city commissioners have not yet formally accepted or rejected the state's enforcement terms. City staff have been negotiating with FDEP to reduce or resolve the thousands of dollars in penalties.

 The enforcement action follows allegations that the city has been operating docks at Little Jim's on state-owned submerged land without authorization. FDEP says the city never had permission to use the land. City Commissioner Michael Broderick acknowledged the allegation on July 6.

 The FDEP action is one of several legal and regulatory pressures surrounding the historic waterfront property. In early July, Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously to reject a settlement offer in a lawsuit filed by local resident Kevin Keene, who alleged years of waterfront mismanagement tied to Little Jim's. The city has filed a motion to dismiss Keene's amended complaint.

 Keene said he will continue to pursue litigation. Broderick said the city is planning to hire a real estate manager to oversee development decisions and prevent future situations.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Planning & Zoning Board recommends Miracle Mile extension for former Doctors Clinic site
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended the City Council change the land use of a seven-acre parcel at 2300 5th Ave. from residential to commercial for mixed-use development.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Planning & Zoning Board unanimously recommended July 16 that the City Council change the land use of a seven-acre parcel from residential to commercial so a developer can repurpose the property at 2300 5th Ave. for mixed-use development as part of a northern extension of the Miracle Mile Business District. The applicant, 2300 5th Avenue LLC, has purchased an office building known locally as the Doctors Clinic. Through redevelopment, the site is planned to become integrated into the Miracle Mile area.

 Principal Planner Cheri Fitzgerald said the request would change the future land use map from residential medium to commercial. The property is currently an office and pre-school. The amendment would extend the Miracle Mile commercial district to the north, which would allow mixed-use residential and commercial uses that could better align with more recent development trends. Fitzgerald based her recommendation of approval on the application's compliance with city code.

 Contracted Land Planner Rebecca Grohall said the site was originally the Doctors Clinic specialized in healthcare, but many specialty medical practices eventually migrated toward the hospital. Today, it is generally utilized as office and a pre-school and faces vacancy rates and under-utilization. Grohall said the site plan has not been started because the Commercial Land Use designation is needed first.

 Possibilities include a hotel, multifamily units, and a true mixed-use development with ground-floor retail and upper floor residential uses. The Planning & Zoning Board voted 4-0 to recommend approval.

The Fort Pierce Police Department is searching for a driver who struck two children with a car on Saturday and left the scene before authorities arrived. The crash happened on 25th Street near the Elks Lodge in Fort Pierce.

 Investigators said the driver, believed to be between 20 and 30 years old, stopped briefly to check on the children after the crash but then drove away. Police are looking for a gold Mercedes-Benz that may have damage to the driver's side.

 One of the children was taken to a hospital with injuries that were not considered life-threatening. The condition of the second child has not been released.

 Anyone with information about the driver or the vehicle is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.

cards.headline: Fort Myers man arrested after road rage PIT maneuver crashes family's SUV into fence on I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: A Fort Myers man is charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and child abuse after deputies say he performed a PIT maneuver on a North Carolina family's vehicle during a road rage incident near Stuart.
cards.body:
Michael Jeffrey Spiers, 36, was arrested Saturday night after he allegedly used a PIT maneuver to send a North Carolina family's SUV into a barbed-wire fence during a road rage attack near Kanner Highway and I-95. The crash happened around 7:30 p.m. Saturday. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident involved a woman traveling alone and her brother, his wife, and their young son following in another vehicle while on vacation from North Carolina.

 Investigators said Spiers first went after the woman, chasing her through a gas station parking lot before following her onto the highway and repeatedly trying to force her off the road. The woman called 911, and Spiers then turned his attention to the family's vehicle. Witnesses reported Spiers was flailing his arms and making what appeared to be gang signs during the encounters.

 Spiers intentionally performed a PIT maneuver on the family's car, sending the SUV spinning off 96th Street near Kanner Highway and crashing into a barbed-wire fence. The three family members ran from the car and hid in the brush until deputies arrived.

 Spiers drove to the nearby Sunoco gas station at Kanner Highway and 96th Street where deputies took him into custody. Deputies found a dog inside Spiers' vehicle that had allegedly been stolen in December from someone Spiers used to date. The dog has been reunited with its owner. Spiers remains jailed on charges of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, child abuse and reckless driving.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast homeowners say door-to-door solar sales left them with decades of debt and malfunctioning systems
cards.teaser: Several Treasure Coast homeowners told WPTV they were sold solar systems through door-to-door sales with the expectation of significantly reduced electric bills, but were left with financial obligations ranging from $40,000 to $60,000 lasting as long as 25 years.
cards.body:
Several Treasure Coast homeowners said door-to-door solar pitches left them with decades of debt, malfunctioning systems and power bills that never disappeared. What began with a knock at the door ended for homeowners with financial obligations ranging from $40,000 to $60,000 and lasting as long as 25 years. The homeowners told WPTV they were sold on the expectation that solar panels would significantly reduce or eliminate their electric bills. Instead, some said they were left with malfunctioning systems, continued utility costs and solar companies that later dissolved or filed for bankruptcy.

 Documents Ana Perez shared with WPTV show she leased a roughly $40,000 solar system in November 2021. She said her monthly Florida Power & Light bill initially dropped from about $100 to approximately $30. That changed in the spring of 2026, when her bill climbed up to $131.

 When Perez called FPL, they told her the system had been down since the end of February. By July, bills reviewed by WPTV showed Perez was paying nearly $300 a month, about $150 to FPL and another $150 for the solar lease. That was roughly three times what she said she had paid before installing the panels.

 When Perez tried to have the system repaired under its 10-year warranty, she learned the installer had gone out of business. Records obtained from the Florida attorney general's office show nearly 750 consumer complaints have been filed against just three solar companies featured in WPTV's investigation.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County cities push for more trees and shade as extreme heat bakes neighborhoods
hero.teaser: Palm Beach County Parks and Recreation says the number one need they hear from people, aside from beach access, is shade. Community Greening, a South Florida nonprofit, says adequa
hero.body:
Palm Beach County Parks and Recreation says the number one need they hear from people, aside from beach access, is shade. Community Greening, a South Florida nonprofit, says adequate tree canopy coverage is around the 30 to 40 percent range and virtually every city in Palm Beach County is at least in the 20 percent range and most are lower. The nonprofit has helped plant and give away nearly 30,000 trees across Palm Beach, Broward and parts of Martin County over the past decade.

 Neighborhoods that have adequate tree canopy coverage are on average 7 to 10 degrees cooler than the neighborhoods right next to them that don't have that adequate tree canopy coverage, including at nighttime once the sun is out of the way, according to Josh Weiner, director of communications and engagement for Community Greening. Palm Beach County Parks and Recreation recently partnered with Community Greening to plant 1,000 trees at Dyer Park in West Palm Beach. The county has also started installing additional shade structures, including new coverings over bleachers at Sandalfoot Cove Park in Boca Raton.

 The Resilient Glades Tree Campaign aimed to revitalize tree canopy coverage in South Bay, Belle Glade, Pahokee and Canal Point by planting 2,000 trees at county parks and hosting eight giveaway events. The project was expected to receive roughly $1 million before funding was cut by the Environmental Protection Agency. Community Greening next tree giveaway is scheduled for September at Halpatiokee Regional Park in Martin County. The nonprofit is also partnering with the city of Boca Raton to plant 100 native shade trees along El Rio Trail in September.

cards.headline: South Florida communities weigh data center moratoriums as residents report constant noise from cooling fans
cards.teaser: Multiple municipalities in the Treasure Coast region are exploring or enacting moratoriums on data center construction ahead of the August primary elections.
cards.body:
The debate over constructing massive artificial intelligence data centers is intensifying across South Florida ahead of the August primary elections, as proposals like Project Tango in Palm Beach County draw both interest and opposition. Multiple municipalities in the region are exploring or enacting moratoriums on data center construction. While Florida currently has no hyperscale AI centers, residents living near large-scale data centers in other parts of the country report a constant, industrial hum from cooling fans that operate 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

 Mehran Basiratmand, the Director of Innovations and Programs at Florida Atlantic University and former policy board chairperson for the state's largest data center, said the noise level, the water consumption and electricity impact to surrounding neighborhoods are creating concerns. Basiratmand said these concerns have a legitimate basis, noting the demand is growing and AI is front and center, but officials need to also be equally responsible for the limited resources that are currently available.

 Several cities and counties in the region are either discussing or have already passed temporary bans, or moratoriums, on the approval of new data centers. These measures are designed to give officials time to study the potential impacts and develop zoning and regulatory frameworks that could mitigate issues like noise and resource consumption before developers break ground.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County schools open Aug. 10 with new Tradition Lakes K-8 campus and AI courses
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Public Schools will open for students on Aug. 10 with enrollment expected to hold steady at 42,505 students, though the district is adding new facilities and progr
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Public Schools will open for students on Aug. 10 with enrollment expected to hold steady at 42,505 students, though the district is adding new facilities and programs. Tradition Lakes K-8 will welcome students in western St. Lucie County as the district's newest campus, serving the Tradition area where population growth has been expanding. Superintendent Jon Prince said enrollment is projected to remain flat this year after the district lost 150 students last year instead of gaining the 350 projected by the state, costing around $14 million in state and federal funding.

 The district's tentative budget is $1.07 billion, nearly $60 million less than last year's final budget. Prince said the district made significant cuts, most at the district level rather than directly impacting schools, and no staff were laid off but were instead moved to other positions. Despite the budget reduction, the district is adding two new artificial intelligence courses at Legacy High School this year.

 Over the past seven years, enrollment in St. Lucie County Public Schools has increased by 7 percent, but Prince attributes this year's plateau to more families choosing homeschooling or private schools. Families are already preparing for the first day. Parent Jovani Taylor said he has been purchasing school supplies, books and clothing for his daughter Jayla, who will be starting fourth grade. Another parent, Julia Lopez, said her daughter will be starting VPK and noted the district's growth, saying she sees schools like almost every corner.

 Prince said the district expects as many as 1,600 students at Tradition Lakes K-8 on opening day, with many families benefiting from the school's convenient location in an area of very expansive growth. Principal Latanya Greene said the school's motto is 'Traditions begin here,' reflecting the focus on building a foundation of achievements and accomplishments. Greene said success will be measured not only by academics but also by the sense of community created during the school's inaugural year.

cards.headline: King's Landing development in Fort Pierce advances with luxury villas nearing completion, Marriott Hotel planned for 2029
cards.teaser: The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with construction milestones on ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage,
cards.body:
The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with construction milestones on ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a hotel. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, said construction is nearly complete on Villas 9 and 10, with foundations already in place for Villas 7 and 8.

 Two residences have been sold and are nearing completion. A Marriott Hotel will be part of the development after the company signed an agreement.

 The project sits in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown Fort Pierce. Harris said the location connects downtown to Edgartown and provides walkability to shopping, restaurants, and retail. Residents with boats can store them at the marina.

 Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, said the development could have significant impact on local businesses by bringing in visitors and giving residents a place for their families to stay. She said the downtown area will become an experience where people can walk, shop, live, and play.

 Business owners said having more residents downtown will benefit the area because most amenities are within walking distance. Chaffee Cavalcanti said people can walk to a restaurant and then go to another business to shop and get information. Officials said the estimated completion date is November 2029.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie apartment residents report unanswered maintenance requests, mold at Sanctuary at Winterlakes
cards.teaser: Residents at Sanctuary at Winterlakes Apartments in Port St. Lucie said they have been living with unresolved maintenance issues and that their requests for help are being ignored.
cards.body:
Residents at Sanctuary at Winterlakes Apartments in Port St. Lucie said they have been living with unresolved maintenance issues and that their requests for help are being ignored. Alison Malio walked through her apartment pointing out what she believes is structural damage in her bedroom and damage she described as rot near the foundation. She also said her freezer seal was damaged and has cost her over $1,500 in lost food over the last year and a half to two years. Malio also showed a cockroach problem inside her apartment and building and said pest control only comes once every 13 weeks.

 Malio said she and her neighbors submit maintenance requests through an online portal, but she claims those requests go unanswered or get deleted and are sometimes marked complete even when no work has been done. Malio said she has cameras and a ring doorbell so she knows if maintenance comes to look at issues. She said it has been six or seven years of the property management doing nothing to help residents.

 Across the parking lot, neighbor Cheryl Jones said her air conditioning was out for nine weeks. Jones said it was too hot in her apartment to cook and she could only make breakfast with her coffee maker and toaster. Jones said maintenance eventually fixed the air conditioning, but mold had grown inside her apartment.

 Jones sent a report from a company that tested her unit and found evidence of mold, recommending that drywall, insulation and other materials be removed. Jones said she sent that report to property management but has not heard anything back.

 Property management sent a statement saying they are looking into the issues and that they prioritize the safety and well-being of tenants. When asked why they do not move, both Malio and Jones said they cannot afford to go anywhere else. Jones said she has nowhere to go.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents oppose proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe over concerns for St. Lucie County Regional History Museum
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the area's cultural heritage and the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum. Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County's history, expressed disbelief over the proposed changes.

 This is a gem for the area, and I just can't believe they want to put mega yachts here, he said. The museum, it's our culture. It's the center for our culture for this county.

 In a statement, St. Lucie County said that no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings. This is just a really fantastic place, and our history is capsulized in this museum here, he said. The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce pizza shop transforms patio into free reading room for children
cards.teaser: Big Apple Pizza in Fort Pierce is converting its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up free books any time they visit. Owner Scott Van Duzer has op
cards.body:
Big Apple Pizza in Fort Pierce is converting its outdoor patio into a dedicated reading room where children can pick up free books any time they visit. Owner Scott Van Duzer has operated a free book program inside the restaurant for years, but the collection has grown too large for the indoor space.

 Van Duzer said the patio transformation addresses the space shortage while making books more accessible to young readers. Children can take home any book they want at no charge, whether their family stops in for pizza or just to browse the collection. The program aims to encourage a lifelong love of reading and remove barriers to book access.

 Van Duzer said his commitment to giving back stems from lessons he learned from his mother while growing up. He said she taught him that if he could give back, he should give back, and the restaurant lives that principle every day. Watching children get excited about discovering new books has been one of the most rewarding parts of the program.

 Construction on the reading room is underway and is expected to be completed later this fall. Until then, children can continue picking up free books inside Big Apple Pizza at 2311 S 35th St in Fort Pierce, where every child remains welcome to take a book home.

hero.headline: PSL Mets score three in 10th to beat Blue Jays 6-3
hero.teaser: John Smith III reached base four times and scored a key insurance run as St. Lucie snapped a three-game losing streak with an extra-inning win in Dunedin.
hero.body:
The St. Lucie Mets scored three runs in the 10th inning Saturday night to defeat the Dunedin Blue Jays 6-3 at TD Ballpark.

The extra-inning victory snapped St. Lucie’s three-game losing streak and improved the Mets to 3-1 in extra-inning games this season. Dunedin rallied twice during regulation to tie the game but never took the lead.

Ryan Tayman opened the scoring with a two-run double in the first inning, giving St. Lucie an early 2-0 advantage. JoJo Parker tied the game with a two-run home run in the sixth.

The Mets regained the lead in the seventh when Elian Peña scored on a two-out RBI infield single by John Smith III.

St. Lucie carried a 3-2 lead into the bottom of the ninth, but the Blue Jays loaded the bases with no outs against Elwis Mijares. Zack Mack entered from the bullpen and limited Dunedin to a sacrifice fly, sending the game to extra innings tied 3-3.

Peña advanced to third on a wild pitch by Noah Palmese in the top of the 10th before Wyatt Vincent delivered a sacrifice fly to put the Mets back in front.

Smith III was then hit by a pitch and later scored on another Palmese wild pitch, extending the lead to 5-3. Julio Zayas followed with an RBI single to bring home St. Lucie’s final run.

Mack retired the Blue Jays in the bottom of the 10th and induced a game-ending groundout from Jake Cook, who represented the potential tying run. Mack earned the victory after pitching two scoreless innings.

Smith III finished 2-for-3 with two singles, a walk and a hit-by-pitch. He drove in one run, scored twice and reached base in four of his five plate appearances.

Mets starter Nate Hall allowed one hit over three scoreless innings and recorded one strikeout. Jonathan Jimenez added 2⅓ scoreless innings with four strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 13-21 in the second half and 46-54 overall. The Blue Jays fell to 17-17 in the second half and 47-52 overall.

St. Lucie and Dunedin will conclude their six-game series Sunday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for noon, with the Mets seeking their second 3-3 series split of the season.

cards.headline: Blue Jays score five in eighth to shut out St. Lucie Mets 5-0
cards.teaser: Ethan Lanthier and Christian Rodriguez held Dunedin scoreless through seven innings, but the Blue Jays broke through with five runs in the eighth to hand St. Lucie its third straight loss in the series.
cards.body:
DUNEDIN — A scoreless pitchers' duel unraveled for the St. Lucie Mets in the eighth inning Friday night as the Dunedin Blue Jays scored five runs and pulled away for a 5-0 victory at TD Ballpark.

 The loss was St. Lucie's third straight in the series. The Mets kept Dunedin off the scoreboard through seven innings behind strong outings from starter Ethan Lanthier and reliever Christian Rodriguez, but the Blue Jays sent eight batters to the plate during the decisive eighth.

 Lanthier delivered four scoreless innings, allowing one hit. Rodriguez followed with three hitless frames before running into trouble in his fourth inning of work.

 The eighth began when Rodriguez walked No. 9 hitter Brayden Martin, who reached on walks in all three of his plate appearances. Rodriguez then hit Jake Cook with a pitch. Blaine Bullard and Ryan Cooney followed with consecutive RBI singles to give Dunedin a 2-0 lead.

 With two outs, Jake Bennett doubled over the first-base bag to drive in two more runs. Enmanuel Bonilla scored from third on a wild pitch to complete the five-run inning.

 Rodriguez was charged with five runs on three hits over four innings and took the loss.

 Dunedin starter Carson Messina struck out seven over a season-high 4 2/3 innings without issuing a walk. Reese Bassinger retired all four batters he faced, Landen Waters worked a perfect seventh and Josbel Garcia pitched the final two innings to complete the shutout and earn the win.

 The Mets finished with five hits from five players. Simon Juan went 1-for-4 with a triple, while Aiden Robbins reached base three times with a single, a walk and a hit-by-pitch.

 St. Lucie fell to 12-21 in the second half and 45-54 overall. Dunedin improved to 17-16 in the second half and 47-51 overall.

 The teams continue the series Saturday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Blue Jays outlast St. Lucie Mets 14-9 in Dunedin slugfest
cards.teaser: Yovanny Rodriguez and Bohan Adderley hit their first St. Lucie home runs, but Dunedin scored six unanswered runs after the Mets briefly took a 9-8 lead.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets hit three home runs and briefly rallied into the lead Wednesday night, but the Dunedin Blue Jays scored six unanswered runs over the final three innings to win 14-9 at TD Ballpark.

 The loss evened the series at one game apiece. St. Lucie has scored 51 runs over its last five games but has allowed 52, going 2-3 during that stretch.

 Yovanny Rodriguez gave the Mets a 3-0 lead in the first inning with a three-run homer, his first since joining St. Lucie from the Florida Complex League.

 Dunedin answered quickly. JoJo Parker hit a two-run homer off Owen Woodward in the bottom of the first, then connected for another two-run shot against Jose Lopez in the second. Parker, the Blue Jays’ top prospect, finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk, four RBIs and four runs scored.

 St. Lucie trailed 8-6 entering the fifth before Simon Juan and Bohan Adderley hit back-to-back home runs with two outs. Juan’s two-run shot tied the game, and Adderley followed with his first St. Lucie homer to put the Mets ahead 9-8.

 The lead held until the seventh, when Dunedin scored four runs against reliever Zack Mack. Parker opened the rally with a hard infield single that first baseman Branny De Oleo stopped, but De Oleo’s throw toward second base escaped into the outfield and allowed Jake Cook to score the tying run.

 Juan Sanchez then chopped a two-run single to give the Blue Jays an 11-9 lead and later scored on a wild pitch. Dunedin added two more runs in the eighth on RBI singles by Brayden Martin and Blaine Bullard.

 After Adderley’s go-ahead homer, Dunedin relievers Noah Palmese, Ricky Tiedemann, Isaac Williams and Dax Dathe combined to retire 10 consecutive Mets batters.

 Elian Peña ended that streak with a leadoff single in the ninth and reached third on an error with no outs. The Mets had a chance to score in double figures for a fourth consecutive game, but Bradley Wilson struck out three straight batters to strand Peña at third.

 Peña went 2-for-4 with two singles and two RBIs, while Adderley finished 2-for-4. Eight of St. Lucie’s nine starters recorded at least one hit.

 Dylan Carey, an undrafted free agent from Nebraska, made his professional debut and went 1-for-3 with a single, a hit-by-pitch and a run scored. He also played error-free defense at shortstop.

 Elwis Mijares provided the strongest outing from the Mets bullpen, pitching 2⅓ scoreless innings with three strikeouts. Woodward, pitching on a minor league rehabilitation assignment, worked the first inning and ended his appearance with consecutive strikeouts.

 Lopez followed Woodward and allowed six runs on four hits and six walks over 2⅔ innings. Mack took the loss after being charged with four runs in two-thirds of an inning.

 Sanchez finished 2-for-4 with a double, two walks and four RBIs for Dunedin. Cook reached base in each of his final five plate appearances with three singles and two walks.

 The Mets fell to 12-19 in the second half and 45-52 overall. The Blue Jays improved to 14-17 in the second half and 45-51 overall.

 The teams play the third game of the series Thursday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
cards.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
cards.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

 Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

 The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

 Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

 Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

 Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

 The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

 Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

 Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

 Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

 Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

 The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

 Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

 The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

 The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named FSL Pitcher of the Week
cards.teaser: The 22-year-old left-hander struck out 12 batters over seven scoreless innings in two appearances against Fort Myers.
cards.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced Monday.

 Ware made two appearances against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Clover Park, starting Tuesday and returning for a relief outing Sunday. The left-hander combined to throw seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two walks while striking out 12 batters.

 The Mets won both games in which Ware appeared. He earned the victory Sunday after pitching four scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk and recording a career-high eight strikeouts as St. Lucie rallied for an 11-8 win.

 Ware, 22, was selected by the New York Mets in the 15th round of the 2025 MLB Draft out of LSU. He made his professional debut with St. Lucie in April and has remained with the team throughout the season.

cards.headline: Mets erase 5-0 deficit to beat Mighty Mussels 11-8
cards.teaser: Jeremy Rodriguez went 4-for-4, and Conner Ware struck out a career-high eight as St. Lucie scored eight runs in the second inning.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets erased an early five-run deficit with an eight-run second inning and rallied for an 11-8 win over the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Sunday afternoon at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers won the seven-game series 4-3 and finished the season series with an 8-4 advantage.

 The Mighty Mussels scored three runs in the first inning and two more in the second to build a 5-0 lead. St. Lucie responded with eight runs in the bottom of the second and moved ahead for good.

 Randy Guzman delivered the decisive hit, lining a two-out, two-run single that turned a 5-4 deficit into a 6-5 Mets lead. Julio Zayas followed with a two-run single to extend the advantage to 8-5.

 The Mets added three runs in the third. Elian Peña hit an RBI single, Jacob Reimer drove in a run with a double and Trey Snyder added a sacrifice fly to make it 11-5.

 Conner Ware took over on the mound in the third inning and settled the game down for St. Lucie. Ware pitched four scoreless innings, allowed one hit and one walk, and struck out a career-high eight batters. He struck out the side swinging in the fourth and struck out the side looking in the sixth before earning the win.

 Fort Myers scored three runs in the seventh against Luis Sotillo, who was making his Mets debut. Sotillo recovered by retiring six of the final seven batters he faced and carried the game through the eighth inning.

 Elwis Mijares worked a perfect ninth on six pitches to record his third save.

 Jeremy Rodriguez led the Mets at the plate, going 4-for-4 with a double, an RBI and two runs scored from the No. 9 spot in the order. Zayas and Peña collected two hits apiece.

 Reimer, beginning a minor league rehabilitation assignment for a groin injury, went 1-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and two runs scored. He played all nine innings at third base.

 The Mets improved to 11-18 in the second half and 44-51 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game road series against the Dunedin Blue Jays on Tuesday. First pitch at TD Ballpark is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Fall Short in 15-14 Loss to Fort Myers
cards.teaser: Randy Guzman hit two home runs and drove in six as the St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run deficit in a 15-14 loss to Fort Myers.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run first-inning deficit but fell one run short in a 15-14 loss to the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Saturday night at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers scored eight runs in the opening inning and survived several St. Lucie rallies to earn its third consecutive victory.

 Mets starter Ethan Lanthier was charged with seven runs on five hits and two walks before being removed with two outs in the first inning. Harry Genth delivered a three-run double during the Mussels' early outburst.

 Mets Answer With Five-Run First Inning

 St. Lucie immediately responded with five runs against Fort Myers starter Matt Barr in the bottom of the first. Antonio Jimenez, Branny De Oleo and Simon Juan each recorded RBI hits to cut the deficit to 8-5.

 The Mighty Mussels added three runs against Franyel Diaz in the third inning. Ramiro Dominguez drove in two with a single, and Byron Chourio hit a solo home run to extend the Fort Myers lead to 11-5.

 Trey Snyder helped St. Lucie pull closer in the fourth inning with an unconventional trip around the bases. Snyder's ground-ball single was mishandled by shortstop Quetin Young, who then committed a throwing error that allowed Snyder to score and another run to cross the plate.

 The play cut the Mussels' lead to 11-7.

 Guzman Homers Twice

 Randy Guzman hit a two-run homer against Ramiro Villanueva in the fifth inning to bring the Mets within two runs.

 Villanueva later hit consecutive batters and was ejected. St. Lucie loaded the bases with one out, but reliever Adam Falinski retired Elian Pena on a popout and Snyder on a groundout to preserve the 11-9 Fort Myers advantage.

 Young answered with a three-run home run over the batter's eye in the sixth, pushing the Mussels' lead to 14-9.

 Guzman responded again in the bottom half of the inning, launching a three-run homer to make it 14-12.

 He finished the game 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, six RBIs and two runs scored.

 Ninth-Inning Rally Falls One Run Short

 Ricardo Paez opened the ninth inning with a solo home run that gave Fort Myers a 15-13 lead and provided what proved to be a crucial insurance run.

 Francisco Toledo scored on a wild pitch and throwing error with one out in the bottom of the ninth. Marco Vargas then homered to right field with two outs, pulling St. Lucie within one run at 15-14.

 Brent Francisco struck out Chase Meggers to end the game and record his third save.

 Michael Hilker Jr. earned the win after pitching 2 1/3 scoreless innings of relief for Fort Myers. Lanthier took the loss.

 Jimenez went 2-for-3 with two walks and three runs scored. Vargas, De Oleo and Juan added two hits apiece.

 The Mets fell to 10-18 in the second half and 43-51 overall. The Mighty Mussels improved to 14-14 in the second half and 51-42 overall.

 The teams will conclude their series Sunday at Clover Park. First pitch is scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

hero.headline: Space Coast Symphony Orchestra brings Landscapes & Legends concert to Vero Beach
hero.teaser: The Space Coast Symphony Orchestra will perform Landscapes Legends on Sunday, August 10, at the Community Church of Vero Beach, 1901 23rd Street. The concert features works explori
hero.body:
The Space Coast Symphony Orchestra will perform Landscapes Legends on Sunday, August 10, at the Community Church of Vero Beach, 1901 23rd Street. The concert features works exploring magic and myth, with guest conductor Patrick Phillips leading the performance.

 The program opens with Dukas' The Sorcerer's Apprentice, the 11-minute orchestral tone poem famously depicted in Disney's Fantasia. The concert includes the world premiere performance of Kenneth Fuchs' Cloud Slant, a work capturing light, motion and atmosphere. Fuchs won the 2018 GRAMMY Award for Best Classical Compendium for an album recorded with the London Symphony Orchestra for Naxos.

 Vero Beach music and arts leader Dr. Jacob Craig will perform Edward MacDowell's Piano Concerto No. 2, a deeply romantic and expressive three-movement work composed in 1885. The work holds the distinction of being the first major piano concerto written by an American. Renowned pianist Van Cliburn chose MacDowell's Piano Concerto No. 2 at age 18 for his professional orchestral debut.

 The concert concludes with Pines of Rome, the 1924 orchestral tone poem by Italian composer Ottorino Respighi. The 22-minute work dramatically depicts four different locations around Rome framed by iconic pine trees. Tickets cost $35 through www.SpaceCoastSymphony.org or at Marine Bank Trust branches, and $40 at the door.

 Concertgoers aged 18 and under or with a college ID are admitted free. For more information, call 855-252-7276.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Museum of Art features American artists, new building exhibit through 2027
cards.teaser: More than 80 works by artists including Benjamin West, John Singer Sargent and Mary Cassatt are on display at Vero Beach Museum of Art through Aug. 16.
cards.body:
An exhibition titled American Made at Vero Beach Museum of Art includes more than 80 works by artists including Benjamin West, Sarah Miriam Peale, Edward Moran, John Singer Sargent, Mary Cassatt, Robert Henri and Charles Alston. The exhibit runs through Aug. 16 at the Holmes and Titelman Galleries at 3001 Riverside Park Drive in Vero Beach.

 Another exhibit, James Prosek: At Work, is on display at the museum's Holmes Gallery through Oct. 25. The exhibit features projects which define the artist's first 30 years of artmaking. Admission is free to members, children 17 and younger, and military veterans and active duty military with valid ID. Admission is $12 for adults, $11 for seniors and $5 for students with ID.

 The museum is also displaying Envisioning the New VBMA, an exhibit tracing the evolution of designs for the museum's new building and transformed campus created by Allied Works architecture and Unknown Studio Landscape Architecture Urban Design. That exhibit runs through Jan. 3, 2027.

cards.headline: TCT’s 2026 Summer Reading Picks: 12 Books to Add to Your List
cards.teaser: From brand-new memoirs and literary thrillers to romance, historical fiction and enduring American classics, these 12 books offer a summer reading option for nearly every mood.

cards.headline: Big Brothers Big Sisters returns Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser to Stuart
cards.teaser: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will hold the Big Taste of Martin County food and spirits event October 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart to support mentoring programs.
cards.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties is preparing for the return of Big Taste of Martin County, a food and spirits event scheduled for October 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast. Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights.

 The event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big, according to Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties. The nonprofit said community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor. cards.headline: Vero Beach Museum of Art to host recycled fishing line bracelet workshop Aug. 8
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Museum of Art and Coastal Connections will team up for a free Second Saturday program starting at 10 a.m. Aug. 8.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Museum of Art and Coastal Connections will host a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8, with hands-on activities, gallery tours and lessons about protecting local marine life. Coastal Connections will lead a hands-on activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium, where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways.

 Participants also can learn about the Fishing Line Recycling Program. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp. From 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., families can take short, docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program.

 Visitors can then participate in Nature in Layers, an art activity for children connected to the museum's exhibitions. Guests also can tour the museum's summer exhibitions throughout the day. James Prosek: At Work is on view in the Holmes Gallery, while Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases is displayed in the Schumann and Titelman galleries. Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day.
